title: A talking cat recommends a Haruki Murakami novel
dek: No plot summaries, no reading order. Twelve questions about wells, cats, jazz and 2am kitchens, and the cat will pick the book.

questions.prompt: It's 2am and the fridge is the only light. You:

options.label: Cook spaghetti and think about someone who left
Follow the cat. It clearly knows something
Take the lift to a floor that shouldn't exist
Sit in a diner until the city goes quiet

results.name: Norwegian Wood
results.tagline: The one about the person you didn't save
results.blurb: Your book is the quiet one, the one people dismiss as his simple novel and then can't stop thinking about. It's about memory, rain, a record on repeat and the specific ache of loving someone who is already leaving. You read for the mood and you know exactly which page undoes you.
strengths: Sits with grief instead of solving it
results.watchOut: You keep replaying the same year. The record has another side.

results.name: Kafka on the Shore
results.tagline: Two stories, one cat, no explanation
results.blurb: Your novel has a boy, an old man, a cat who talks and a rule that makes no sense until it does. You like stories that behave like dreams and trust you to keep up. You are less interested in what happened than in what it felt like at 3am.
strengths: Follows an instinct past the map
results.watchOut: You let mystery excuse the hard conversation. Some things do have answers.

results.name: The Wind-Up Bird Chronicle
results.tagline: A well, a cat, and a very long war
results.blurb: You want the big, patient book: the one with a well you climb down into, a marriage coming apart, and history bleeding into a suburban kitchen. You are willing to sit in something slow and unsettling until it tells you what it means.
strengths: Connects the personal to the historical
Not frightened by a long silence
results.watchOut: You go down the well alone and stay too long. Bring a rope.

results.name: 1Q84
results.tagline: Two moons, two lives, one enormous book
results.blurb: You like your fiction with architecture: parallel lives, a made-up year, a cult, a killer, and a plot that clicks together like a mechanism. You are happy to carry a very heavy book because you want to live inside the system, not just visit it.
strengths: Loves a structure that pays off
results.watchOut: You'll follow the plot and miss the person beside you. Look up at the real moon.

results.name: Hard-Boiled Wonderland and the End of the World
results.tagline: Two worlds, one head, no way out
results.blurb: Your favourite is the strange early one: a split narrative, a job with no explanation, and a town where people lose their shadows. You like a book that builds a machine and dares you to work out what it's for.
results.watchOut: You can admire the mechanism and forget to feel anything. Read the last chapter twice.

results.name: Colorless Tsukuru Tazaki and His Years of Pilgrimage
results.tagline: The friend group that closed without explanation
results.blurb: Your novel is about being cut off by people you loved and then, years later, going back to ask why. You are the one who needs the reason, the closure, the conversation everyone else has moved past. You are also the one who will actually make the trip.
results.watchOut: Not every ending has a reason you can collect. Sometimes the answer is just time.

results.name: After Dark
results.tagline: One night, one city, everyone awake
results.blurb: Your book is a single night in a city, told from a slight distance, with a diner, a bass player, a hotel room and a girl who doesn't want to go home. You like atmosphere over plot and you have never entirely trusted daylight.
strengths: At home in the in-between hours
Notices what a room feels like
results.watchOut: You watch the night from a slight distance. Sit at the table sometime.
